subject: Simulations using groups for specifying sex-specific parameters

messages.author: 91bd4367f6044e8d
messages.subject: Simulations using groups for specifying sex-specific parameters
parts:
Hi Murray,

I'm running some simulations to test some new proposed trap layouts with different parameters for males and females. Here is my code (using the example given in the secrdesign vignette, thanks for that).

library(secrdesign)
library(rgdal)
ciArea <- readOGR("ChurchillIs_1m_elev_area.shp")
ciScenarios <- make.scenarios(D = 0.944, g0 = 0.3, sigma = 30, noccasions = c(3,4), groups = c('F', 'M'), detectfn = "HR")
male <- ciScenarios$group == 'M'
ciScenarios$D[male] <- 1.847
ciScenarios$g0[male] <- 0.4
ciScenarios$sigma[male] <- 35
ciScenarios[,1:8]
ciGrid <- read.traps("ciTraps.txt")
ciMask <- make.mask(ciGrid, buffer = 160, type = "trapbuffer", poly = ciArea)
exfn <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, 'secr') & !is.null(x$fit)) {
    pred <- predict(x)
    pred[[1]][c('D','pmix'),]
  }
  else data.frame()
}
rawCiScen <- run.scenarios(100, ciScenarios, trapset = list(ciGrid))
summary(rawCiScen)
ciSims <- run.scenarios(100, scenarios = ciScenarios, trapset = list(ciGrid), fit = TRUE,
                        extractfn = exfn, fit.args = list(model = list(g0~h2, sigma~h2),
                        hcov = 'group'), maskset = list(ciMask))
summary(select.stats(ciSims, 'D'))$OUTPUT
summary(select.stats(ciSims, 'pmix'))$OUTPUT

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Simulations using groups for specifying sex-specific parameters
parts:
Hi again

Were you really needing to use detectfn = 'HR'? That is the source of the trouble.
1. When you simulate data with detectfn='HR' but do not specify the third parameter z, sim.capthist (called by run.scenarios) defaults to z = 1. With your other settings that results in a very fat tail, truncated at the mask buffer radius.
2. The fat tail results in very large numbers of detections - probably more than you really expect.
3. As you do not specify the detectfn to fit, secr.fit (again called by run.scenarios) defaults to HN. However the "true" HR value of sigma (30 m) is a terrible starting value for the HN sigma needed to model the flat, wide detections from the HR model with z=1, and the likelihood computation bombs.

I suggest keeping things simple (detectfn='HN' throughout). The alternative is to grapple with the various issues (specifying detectfn in fit.args etc.). Using HR (or HHR) is always risky.

The other warning message can probably be ignored - I'll clean it up in the next release.
Murray
